confirm_schema.note: Machine-suggested from the document header; check it against the Udyam certificate before it becomes the request's supplier name.
The request has no invoice-number field of its own; the invoice reference sits on the INVOICE evidence item, or stays in your records.
Required by the request. The engine anchors nothing on it - delivery does that - but it must be the date on the document.
The value of the supply. Everything the engine computes runs from this figure, so confirm it against the invoice total line.
The request has no supplier GSTIN field. Keep it in your records or on the GST_RETURN evidence reference; there is nothing to map it to.
Buyer GSTIN as printed on the invoice; used only to identify the buyer.
Exactly the name on the invoice's bill-to line, spelling included.
Leave null only if there is genuinely no delivery proof: a missing delivery date blocks Stage 4 and leaves acceptance unresolved (6.2).
The PO number as printed. The request records it as the PO evidence item's reference rather than as a date or an amount.
Only what a written document actually says. Null means no written agreement was supplied; what counts as one is still open (OQ-5).
Use the message's date as delivery_date, and point the DELIVERY_PROOF evidence item's reference at this line of the chat export.
Add an objections[] row: raised_date = the message date, is_written = true (a chat is writing), description = the message text. The engine, not this screen, decides whether it qualifies.

Same row shape as a DEFECT_OBJECTION, but the date falls after the configured objection window, so the engine will record it as a complaint that does not move the clock rather than as a qualifying objection (6.2).
The message date becomes resolved_date on the objection it answers, which is what closes that objection for the engine.
Add an acknowledgments[] row: kind = WHATSAPP_PROMISE, is_signed = false, date = the message date. The engine records it as a promise that does not restart the limitation clock (6.5).

Replacement received, the issue is resolved. Thanks for the quick fix.
Day 24 - finding more damaged cartons in the same lot. This is unacceptable.
Payment for the invoice will be released by 20 March.

warnings.text: Every value and tag in this response was suggested by a machine from the uploaded text, with a line citation and a confidence. Nothing reaches a case evaluation until a person confirms it; the engine never calls this module.

Lateness was assessed against the configured objection window of 15 days from the delivery date, and the config still marks this value unverified (OQ-1, source V2:s.2(b)). A late tag is a suggestion: the engine re-derives the same question from the confirmed request.
Chat dates on line(s) 4, 5, 6, 10 could be read either way. Header dates are read as DD/MM/YYYY (Indian export); check those lines before confirming.
